outputs: coverage_matrix.json maps 24 planned modules, 63 feature-to-case entries, 8 release acceptance criteria and 45 v0.1 test files; states are covered, pending_same_batch, documentation_only or future_gate

the matrix validator resolves every referenced file::test node with AST, requires non-empty test files for covered modules, keeps old test files present, and checks the 29-tool catalog, entry points, import paths and the original mock query
Linux tests use the real file-key backend: 0600 mode, broad permission refusal, symlink refusal, key/data separation, tamper detection and ciphertext without plaintext
Windows tests use the real DPAPI backend and are skipped on Linux with an explicit platform reason; no Windows host result is claimed from the Linux run

the seven-fault matrix covers timeout, lost/cut response, cancellation, lock conflict, process exit, disk full and partial write; every write path has request counters and no uncertain write is replayed
protected-store rotation interruption, pointer-switch failure, ENOSPC, short write and fsync failure keep the previous verified record readable; no temporary file is adopted as a record
lost upload response keeps upload count at one across repeated result reads; prepare sends zero remote writes; a lost submit is resolved by readback, not resend
cursor, cache, media reference and dashboard session are bound to account and scope; cross-account and cross-semester use is refused instead of returning old data

cross-midnight intervals keep their exact start/end and Asia/Shanghai timezone; date-only deadlines stay DATE and never receive midnight; stable ids survive title changes and separate same-title sources
a failed source produces SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with historical carry-forward and zero DELETED; a missing page produces SOURCE_INCOMPLETE and suppresses deletion; neither becomes an empty success

report generator fields: schema, source commit/branch/dirty, product version, contract inventory and set digest, platform/Python/Node, scope, totals, Node totals, module buckets, skip reasons, gaps, failures and side-effect counters
failure records contain only the node id, module, stable error class and a pytest minimal repro; raw exception text, paths, tokens, cookies and account values never enter the report
skip classification: platform hints are explainable, environment hints set the platform INCOMPLETE, unexplained reasons fail the gate; the platform name itself must be known
aggregate requires the requested platforms (linux and windows by default) and one source commit across reports; missing platform or commit mismatch fails

release gate requires test evidence, scans source and every candidate archive with privacy_scan, audits the frozen runtime/dev/Node pins, checks conservative defaults, verifies the candidate and scans the installed wheel for the exact marker set

CI test jobs emit per-platform JUnit, build and upload only safe regression-report JSON, and the release-gate job downloads all platform reports, builds the candidate, runs the gate with marker_set.json and uploads release-gate.json

CI uses fixed Ubuntu 24.04 / Windows 2025, Python 3.12/3.13, Node 24, explicit Chromium installation, read-only contents permission, persist-credentials false and no pull_request_target; no raw logs or secrets are uploaded
docs/MAINTENANCE.md documents report, aggregate and release-gate commands, skip semantics, marker scope and blocking rules

This host is Linux. Windows DPAPI, Windows ACL and Windows session migration cases are skipped with explicit platform reasons. A real Windows result must come from the windows-2025 CI job at the same commit; a skipped case is not a pass and the Windows-shaped report used for local aggregation is not Windows evidence.
Skip classification is policy-based. A new skip reason outside the platform/environment hints fails the gate until it is explained; this is intentional, not an omission.

Exact marker scanning covers the installed wheel only. The source archive and sdist intentionally include tests and marker_set.json, so privacy_scan.py's generic credential/sensitive-file rules cover them; scanning those archives for the committed marker definitions would self-report the definitions as leaks.
Fault injection uses the 5.3 synthetic submission transport and temporary 2.2 keys. No production upload endpoint, real account or real campus write exists in this module.

The local API timeout case uses a 0.15 s deadline and a non-cooperative facade; the worker thread may outlive the request until process exit, which is the 6.2 documented process boundary, not a new cancellation capability.

The report keeps only error classes and repository-relative node ids. Skip reasons and findings are path/token sanitized, but the report is an engineering summary, not a general data-loss-prevention system.

The local release-gate pass used a real Linux JUnit plus a Windows-shaped report at the same commit to exercise aggregation. The two-platform CI result remains to be observed and recorded by 8.1 at the integration commit.
The candidate package is a local candidate build, not a release. No main merge, tag or GitHub Release was created.
regression_report.py adds no runtime dependency and uses the existing pinned Python/Node runtimes and the explicit Chromium install.
